references.text: Describes the fat to be offered from the peace offering, including the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—the same fatty parts mentioned in Leviticus 9:19.

Specifically regarding the sheep as a peace offering, it mentions the fat tail (alyah), the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—identical parts to those in Leviticus 9:19.
Describes the fatty parts from the sin offering that are to be removed and offered, including the kidneys and the lobe of the liver, corresponding to the fat mentioned in Leviticus 9:19.
Refers to the fatty parts from the guilt offering that are to be offered: the fat tail, the fat on the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—the same anatomical parts as in Leviticus 9:19.
Moses takes the fat from the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys during the consecration offering—parallel to the fatty parts in Leviticus 9:19.
At the consecration of Aaron, Moses takes the fat, the fat tail, the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys—a direct parallel to the list in Leviticus 9:19.
Instructions to take the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys for burning on the altar—the same fatty parts offered in Leviticus 9:19.
From the consecration ram, the fat tail, the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the kidneys are to be taken—identical parts with Leviticus 9:19.
